messages:
jun: Hey all — seeing a spike of 502/connection reset for a few services behind the edge ingress in us-west-2. Starts ~10:12 UTC after a spot drain. Pods are healthy but traffic lands on old node IPs and gets NATed back to a drained node. CoreDNS TTL is 20s, but clients still hit stale IPs. Anyone seen NAT+ingress hairpin like this before?

raj: Which services? clusterIP or headless? Any endpointSlices out of sync?

jun: clusterIP services (ML inference pods). EndpointSlices show endpoints on the new nodes, but kube-proxy iptables rules on some nodes still point to old node IPs.

elaine: Looking at conntrack on one of the edge nodes:
```
# conntrack -L | grep 10.0.5.12
tcp 6 431999 ESTABLISHED src=10.0.5.12 dst=10.0.1.9 sport=56712 dport=443 packets=123 bytes=45678 src=10.0.1.9 dst=10.0.5.12 sport=443 dport=56712 packets=130 bytes=67890 mark=0
```
That dst=10.0.1.9 is a node that was preempted earlier. conntrack entries are persisting and SNAT is sending traffic to the drained node's ENI.

matt: I just saw kube-proxy on the drained node crashlooped during the spot termination. It probably left stale iptables targets on other nodes (hairpin rewrite). Was kube-proxy running in IPVS mode recently?

ops-bot: Autoscaler: terminated instance node-spot-18 (us-west-2a) at 2025-10-14T10:10:32Z.

raj: If kube-proxy crashed while endpoints were moving, other nodes might still have conntrack entries sending traffic to the old node IP. Need to flush conntrack and reconcile endpointslices.

tayla: Proposed safe steps:
1) cordon the remaining edge node that still shows stale mapping (kubectl cordon node-spot-12)
2) drain gracefully if it has pods we can move (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data)
3) force endpointslice controller resync: kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deploy/endpointslice-controller (if managed)
4) restart kube-proxy ds on that AZ: kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart ds/kube-proxy -l topology.kubernetes.io/zone=us-west-2a
5) on nodes that saw hairpin, run: sudo conntrack -D -s <old_node_ip> (or `conntrack -D --orig-dst <old_node_ip>`)

jun: I want to avoid mass conntrack flush because there are ongoing long-lived client connections. Can we target only the stale dst IPs?

elaine: Yeah, target delete by dest IP is safer. Example: `sudo conntrack -D --orig-dst 10.0.1.9` — that'll remove the flows pointing at the drained node. Also worth checking kube-proxy mode: `kubectl get ds kube-proxy -n kube-system -o yaml | grep mode`

matt: Confirmed: kube-proxy on some nodes fell back to iptables mode after the crash. IPVS would have been cleaner here. We should check for mixed-mode drift (some nodes IPVS, some iptables) — that can cause inconsistent endpoint selection.

raj: Action items:
- tayla to cordon/drain the problematic node (us-west-2a) and roll kube-proxy on that zone
- elaine to run targeted conntrack deletes for old node IPs
- matt to run a quick audit of kube-proxy mode across nodes and open a follow-up if mixed modes found
- jun to monitor ingress 5xx rate and CoreDNS logs for retries

tayla: Starting cordon/drain on node-spot-12 now. Will wait for pods to reschedule then restart kube-proxy in that AZ.

elaine: Running targeted conntrack deletes on the three nodes that show traffic to 10.0.1.9 and 10.0.1.11.

ops-bot: k8s: cordon node node-spot-12 — successful.

matt: I pushed a small script to run an audit across the fleet to catch kube-proxy mode mismatches: `scripts/check-kubeproxy-mode.sh` (quick scan shows 3 nodes in us-west-2a reported iptables). I'll open a doc for a longer-term mitigation.

tayla: Rolled kube-proxy ds in us-west-2a, restarted endpointslice controller. Ingress 5xx dropped to baseline within ~45s.

jun: Nice. CoreDNS logs show fewer NXDOMAIN/retries now and client connections are stable.

elaine: Recommend follow-ups:
- add conntrack-targeted cleanup to the spot termination hook (only for flows to the terminated instance IP)
- ensure kube-proxy rollout uses a single mode across the cluster or at least per-zone consistent config
- add an inbound health check at the ingress level that verifies endpoints are reachable at node IPs before adding node to pool

jun: Agreed. Can someone file a small postmortem? I'll take the action to create it and include the above steps.

tayla: Postmortem draft created and linked in #incidents. Marking this incident resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
